purpose: Private independent small-model oracle, separate from all graph cycle/product algorithms and from database authentication.

definition.realTimeOrder: absent; never derived from transaction array order, event seq, ACK time or identifiers
definition.initialization: A distinguished initializer precedes and is visible to every real transaction; it is not counted in the six-transaction capacity.
definition.values: Unique per-key version identities serve as symbolic register values. This is not a repeated-value or arbitrary SQL model.

input.unknownFields: invalid; no silently ignored model/session/clock/evidence options
input.identities: Nonempty Unicode scalar strings, at most 256 UTF-16 units. NUL and all valid control scalars are permitted. Identity uniqueness is per key for versions, and global for transaction IDs.
input.operations: Only point read/write in transaction program order. Zero-operation transactions are explicitly allowed as an observationally empty extension of the paper's nonempty transactions.
input.sources: Every read version must equal its key's initial version or one unique observed write version on that key. Unknown sources are coverage gaps, not invented writes. Transaction-array order is not a source chronology.
input.versionOrders: Every initialized key requires an explicit complete order: initial first, then exactly the last write on that key of every committed writer transaction once each. Intermediate writes remain in ops and source identity; they are not members of final-write order. CO must extend every adjacent pair of these factual orders.
input.orderFacts: The oracle assumes supplied final-write orders are input facts. It does not prove their collection authenticity, infer them from identity/time, complete a missing order, or return a witness order as a capture fact.

coveragePolicy.missingOrPartialOrder: inconclusive even when some independent semantic defect can be noticed
coveragePolicy.unknownOrAbortedOutcome: inconclusive; no opacity and no guessing commit outcome
coveragePolicy.savepointOrRollbackJournal: inconclusive; scoped extension requires a separate contract and must not flatten observations
coveragePolicy.crossKeyFactualOrderCycle: well-formed facts but unsatisfiable abstract execution, not malformed JSON

semantics.INT: At every read, if a previous read or write on the same key exists in that transaction, the returned version equals that last operation's version. A valid read of an own intermediate write remains valid if a later write overwrites it.
semantics.EXT: An initial external read returns the final write to that key of the maximal visible writer under CO, including the initializer. An externally read nonfinal write of another transaction is an explicit EXT/source refutation, kept separate from INT and from any automatic G1b label.
semantics.PREFIX: For one total arbitration/commit order CO, the visibility predecessors of each T are a prefix strictly before T. The initializer is always visible. This directly realizes VIS subset CO and CO;VIS subset VIS.
semantics.NOCONFLICT: For every pair of distinct transactions writing a common key, the CO-earlier writer is visible to the CO-later writer. Blind writes are included.
semantics.serialControl: Use the same point-operation interpretation with every transaction seeing its full CO prefix; TOTALVIS holds. SI-admissible write skew need not be serially admissible.

enumeration.CO: Enumerate every permutation of transaction IDs in Unicode scalar lexicographic order; reject candidates that fail the given final-write orders.
enumeration.cuts: For a transaction at one-based rank r, enumerate prefixLength 0 through r-1 ascending. prefixLength counts real transactions; initializer visibility is implicit. Serial control has only prefixLength=r-1.
enumeration.cutChecks: Check NoConflict, construct the snapshot by applying visible transactions' final writes over explicit initial values, and replay every read/write in original program order.
enumeration.noUnmeteredCartesian: For fixed CO, EXT/INT and NoConflict impose independent requirements on each transaction's cut. Choose a valid cut independently for each transaction; no cross-transaction cut Cartesian product is generated.
enumeration.completenessArgument: PREFIX plus VIS subset a total CO makes each visibility set exactly such a prefix. Every valid abstract execution therefore has an enumerated CO and an enumerated cut for each transaction. Conversely, successful per-transaction replay and shared-writer visibility construct INT/EXT/PREFIX/NoConflict. Cut independence follows because every obligation refers to the fixed CO, fixed final writes and that target transaction's cut, not another transaction's cut.

limits.userBudgets: Any integer from zero through the stated maximum; booleans and larger/negative values are invalid.

states: One before considering each complete CO candidate, including one rejected by factual order.
One before considering each cut candidate, including one rejected by NoConflict or replay.
semanticChecks: One per original operation visited during the INT/source preflight.
One additional source-role inspection for each read; one additional equality comparison if that read has a preceding same-key operation.
One per adjacent pair of each factual version order tested against the candidate CO, including initializer-to-first-writer.
One for each earlier CO transaction inspected for each key written by the cut's target transaction, whether or not that earlier transaction writes that key.
One per initial cell loaded into a candidate snapshot.
One per final-write cell applied from each visible transaction.
One per original operation replayed against a candidate snapshot and one extra comparison per replayed read.
counters.exactExhaustion: Using the final permitted visit does not itself exhaust the budget. A further required visit fails, sets budgetExhausted and returns inconclusive with no witness or no-solution claim.
counters.excludedBoundedWork: JSON parsing, bounded structural/type/source-index completeness validation, Python permutation bookkeeping, scalar map accesses and final report serialization. Limits explicitly bound this excluded input work; counters are semantic work counters, not wall-time or a bound on every VM instruction.
counters.preflight: Coverage/structure validation occurs before semantic decisions. A metered INT or external-intermediate-source refutation may conclude unsatisfiable without enumerating CO, with decisionBasis=axiom-refutation and searchedAllCandidates=false.

output.witness: Only satisfiable results have {kind:'existential-abstract-execution',arbitration:[tx IDs],visibility:[{tx,prefixLength,initializationVisible:true}]}. It is not raw capture evidence and never changes input versionOrders.
output.findings: INT and direct external-intermediate-source facts have separate kinds and original tx/opIndex/source locations. No result is automatically labelled G1b or PL-SI.
output.execution: Effective budgets, actual state/semantic counts, budgetExhausted, searchedAllCandidates and decisionBasis; no witness on invalid/inconclusive/unsatisfiable.
output.absenceWording: Unsatisfiable means no abstract execution for this complete supported finite input and definition, not that a real database is broken for every execution.

primarySources.title: Analysing Snapshot Isolation
primarySources.verifiedBy: Read official authors' PDF with web tool on 2026-10-21. Figure 1 and explanatory INT/EXT/PREFIX/NoConflict text checked; no graph theorem used as oracle decision.

primarySources.purpose: Terminology boundary only: generalized SI permits empty session order; original Adya PL-SI is not substituted.
